_comment: Bus vectors for the DS1307 real-time clock, shared by the tab model (frontend/src/simulation/I2CBusManager.ts, vitest) and the backend twin (backend/app/services/esp32_i2c_slaves.py, pytest). The format is in README.md next to this file. Register facts are from the datasheet, REV 3/15; driver traces name the source they were read from. The host's clock starts every vector at 12:34:56.250 of Wednesday 30 September 2026, and the firmware was built on 29 September 2026 at 23:39:41.

vectors.name: power-on: the clock runs on the host's time, Monday is day 1, CONTROL reads 0x03, the RAM reads 0x00
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Control Register (RS1 and RS0 typically 1 at power-on). CH = 0 and the host's time are the model's: a part that was set and kept its battery. Monday = 1: RTClib dowToDS3231, Seeed DS1307.h MON

vectors.name: a clock nobody set follows the host, its date and its day of week included
vectors.spec: Decision D7: the host clock stays. Datasheet, Clock and Calendar: the day-of-week register increments at midnight

vectors.name: the time is latched at START: a burst that a second ends in the middle of reads one instant
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Clock and Calendar: the user buffers are synchronized to the internal registers on any I2C START; the time is read from these secondary registers while the clock continues to run

vectors.name: the address pointer wraps from 0x3F to 0x00, in a read and in a write
vectors.spec: Datasheet, RTC and RAM Address Map: when the address pointer reaches 3Fh, the end of RAM space, it wraps around to location 00h

vectors.name: the pointer stays where a transfer left it, across the STOP
vectors.spec: Datasheet, I2C Data Bus, data read mode: the first address read is the last one stored in the register pointer. Seeed DS1307::getTime writes the pointer, stops, and then reads

vectors.name: CONTROL and the 56 bytes of RAM keep what is written, and a bit that does not exist reads 0
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Table 2 (0 = always reads back as 0) and Control Register. RTClib RTC_DS1307::writeSqwPinMode, readSqwPinMode (& 0x93), writenvram, readnvram

vectors.name: a time the sketch sets is kept, and the clock counts from the moment the seconds were written
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Clock and Calendar: the divider chain is reset whenever the seconds register is written. Decision D7: a date of the sketch's own is kept

vectors.name: the date rolls over with the month, the year and the leap year, and the day of week with it, from the number the sketch wrote
vectors.spec: Datasheet, General Description: the end of the month date is automatically adjusted for months with fewer than 31 days, including corrections for leap year. Clock and Calendar: the day-of-week values are user-defined but must be sequential

vectors.name: a register written on its own changes that field and leaves the others counting
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Clock and Calendar: the time and calendar are set or initialized by writing the appropriate register bytes

vectors.name: the day of week on its own is a number the sketch gives the day: the time stays the host's
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Clock and Calendar: values that correspond to the day of week are user-defined. DS1307RTC and TimeLib count Sunday as 1

vectors.name: CH stops the clock where it is and reads back, and clearing it starts the clock from there
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Clock and Calendar: bit 7 of register 0 is the clock halt (CH) bit; when set to 1 the oscillator is disabled. RTClib RTC_DS1307::isrunning is !(register 0 >> 7)

vectors.name: a time written while the clock is halted is held, and counts once CH is cleared
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Clock and Calendar: CH. The seconds are written with CH set, then again without

vectors.name: 12-hour mode: the hours count 12, 1 to 11 with AM and PM, in the form they were written in
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Clock and Calendar: bit 6 of the hours register selects the 12-hour mode; in it bit 5 is the AM/PM bit, high being PM

vectors.name: the build time of the firmware, written in one burst, leaves the clock on the host's time
vectors.spec: Decision D7. RTClib 2.1.4 RTC_DS1307::adjust(DateTime(F(__DATE__), F(__TIME__))): pointer 0, seconds, minutes, hours, 0, date, month, year. The day of week is what was written, a day later

vectors.name: one second away from the build time is a date of the sketch's own, and is kept
vectors.spec: Decision D7: the match is on the written date and time, to the second

vectors.name: the build time written one register at a time is the build time once the last one is in
vectors.spec: Decision D7: the rule looks at what the six registers hold when a write phase ends, not at how many bytes the phase had

vectors.name: a date of the sketch's own and then the build time: the clock is back on the host's time
vectors.spec: Decision D7

vectors.name: with no build time known, the time the firmware wrote at build time is kept like any other
vectors.spec: Decision D7: if no compile time can be established for a build, a written time is kept, which is what the chip does

vectors.name: an image with more than one build time: each of them is the build time
vectors.spec: Decision D7. An ESP32 image carries the time of its bootloader and of its application descriptor next to the sketch's, and every date found goes with every time found

vectors.name: the registers a host copies are the time of that moment, CONTROL and the RAM
vectors.spec: dumpRegisters() is what the Raspberry Pi relay mirrors

vectors.name: RTClib RTC_DS1307: begin(), isrunning(), adjust() to a date of the sketch's own, now(), and the NVRAM
vectors.spec: RTClib 2.1.4 RTC_DS1307.cpp with Adafruit BusIO 1.17.4 Adafruit_I2CDevice.cpp: begin() probes the address; read_register writes the pointer, stops, and reads; now() and readnvram() read after a repeated START; adjust() is one write of 8 bytes

vectors.name: Grove RTC DS1307: setTime(), stopClock(), startClock() and getTime(), with Monday as day 1
vectors.spec: Seeed Grove - RTC DS1307 1.0.0, DS1307.cpp: setTime() is one write of 8 bytes, getTime() writes the pointer, stops, and reads 7 bytes, stopClock() and startClock() read the seconds and write them back with CH set or cleared. Example SetTimeAndDisplay: 19 January 2013, 15:28:30, SAT (6)
